v2.3.526 - Fixed a real, deeper cause of Adult Full Library slowness the previous fix didn't fully catch (per direct follow-up report that it was still slow after updating) - all 3 of its parallel-fetch phases (ADE/AFDB static sections, ~135 free-stream-site page fetches, and PandaMovies' own ~160 genre-page fetches) were collecting results from their worker threads in SUBMISSION order instead of completion order, so if even ONE early-submitted fetch was slow that particular run (ordinary site-to-site latency variance), the whole phase blocked on it for up to its full timeout before ever looking at dozens of OTHER jobs that had already finished seconds earlier - confirmed live this is exactly why two loads only 9 minutes apart, same job set, same cache state, measured 13s and 42s: whichever job happened to be slow that run dictated the whole load's time. Now collected in true completion order, so one straggler no longer holds hostage everything that already finished. A genuinely cold cache (nothing fetched before) still costs roughly 25-30s given how many real sources/pages this aggregates from - that part is real network time, not a bug - but every repeat load within the cache window is fast again (confirmed live: 3.6s on a warm cache).

v2.3.517 - Added Vivid TV to Adult's 18+ Channels (adult-tv-channels.click) - confirmed live this one uses a plain static player config with no signing/encryption at all, unlike the DLHD-family channels: its own sourceUrl points directly at a real, currently-airing HLS manifest (live.redtraffic.net/medium.m3u8) with no token or expiry. v2.3.516 - Fixed daddylive.mov being completely dead (confirmed live - DNS/connection failure, not just a down page), which broke NHL/MLB/NBA/NFL Network 24/7 channels in Sports and all 18+ channels in Adult's Channels menu. DaddyLive/DLHD's current mirror is dlstreams.st (this addon already had scraper support for its general SFW channel directory from an earlier session) - confirmed live it preserves the exact same channel_id numbering daddylive.mov always used (id 663 is still "NHL Network USA", 399 still "MLB Network USA", etc.) and resolves through a much simpler mechanism than the old domain's multi-layer XOR/fragment-decode obfuscation, which is now completely gone along with the domain. Rewrote sports_sources.py's channel resolver to look up whatever id/name it's given against dlstreams.st's own catalog and resolve through that, and switched Adult's 18+ channel list from tvnow247.top (whose own channel-data page no longer exposes anything this addon's scraper can find - a separate, unrelated breakage) to dlstreams.st's own real 18+ section (20 real, currently-playable channels, confirmed live). Every existing caller's own function signatures were kept as-is so nothing else needed touching.
v2.3.515 - Reverted the previous release's timeout/limit increases per explicit feedback: raising them did recover more results in testing, but pushed total wait past 45s, which risks looking exactly like "search initiates, nothing ever shows" - just from Kodi's own plugin-call patience running out instead of a code crash. Reduced the per-site fetch cap (15 -> 8) and reverted both the outer unified-search deadline and search_by_title()'s own internal budget back down - a smaller, faster, more reliable first page, leaning on the already-working Next Page pagination for anyone who wants to go deeper, rather than one large, slow, contention-prone request trying to fetch everything at once. Note: while re-verifying this locally, result volume and Next Page behavior both varied significantly between successive test runs against the real live sites - almost certainly this session's own testing (many dozens of rapid repeated requests to the same ~40 real third-party sites while diagnosing this) triggering their own rate-limiting against this specific test connection, not a new code regression. Real-world behavior on a normal, non-hammered connection should be more consistent than what local re-testing showed by the end of this session.
v2.3.514 - Follow-up to the previous release's crash fix: once search actually returned results again, real result volume was still far short of what each site alone provides (confirmed live: 15 streams instead of 430) - instrumented the actual concurrent execution to find why. Adult's unified search runs 6 phases at once (actor/AFDB-title/ADE-title/torrent/stream/myporn), two of which (torrent, stream) each ALSO fan out internally to dozens of sites - all 6 genuinely compete for the same machine's CPU/network simultaneously, so every individual site responds real-world slower under that combined load than any phase's own isolated timing ever showed, and the previous timeouts (tuned against isolated timing) were cutting the stream phase off well before it could finish under real contention. Raised the outer unified-search deadline and the stream phase's own internal budget to give real contention room to complete instead of racing an isolated-case deadline. Confirmed live: the exact same query that returned 15 streams now returns 225 streams across 42 distinct titles - a real, substantial completeness improvement, in exchange for a longer wait (correctness prioritized over speed, per explicit preference).
v2.3.513 - Fixed a real, pre-existing crash behind "Adult search initiates but no results ever show" (confirmed live via a real kodi.log, then reproduced directly): _adult_unified_search_data()'s torrent-title relevance filter referenced a variable (norm_query) that was never actually defined anywhere in that function's own scope - every single search crashed with a NameError the moment torrent results were non-empty, which is common (XXXClub alone regularly matches dozens of real torrents for a query), silently wiping out the ENTIRE search result before anything was ever rendered, real stream/title matches included. This predates every other Adult search fix shipped this session - torrent search has been unconditional here since 2026-08-15, so this has likely been crashing every Adult search that found any torrent matches at all since then. Confirmed live: the exact same query that used to crash now returns real films, torrents, and streams correctly.
v2.3.512 - Follow-up to the previous release's Adult search fix: even with the redundant title-only filters removed, each site's own search contribution was still capped at its first 5 real matches per page (the shared _pfetch() detail-fetch helper's own default), so a genre/performer query with a large real population (confirmed live: watchpornfree.info alone had ~50 real matches for a real performer name) still only surfaced a handful. Raised every active search source's per-page cap from 5 to 15 - confirmed live this took a real performer search from 17 to 50 distinct titles and a real genre search from 33 to 66, both still comfortably inside the search box's own 20s time budget (13-14s measured with a cold cache). Real "Next Page" already existed and works correctly for this screen (confirmed live: a second page call for the same genre query surfaced 60 MORE distinct titles neither request had shown before) - deliberately kept the per-page cap moderate rather than raising it further, since genuinely deeper results are already one Next Page click away rather than needing an ever-larger single request.
v2.3.511 - Fixed the actual root cause of Adult performer/genre search only returning 1-2 movies: two separate title-text-only re-checks (one inside watchpornfree.info's and speedporn.net's own search functions, one in the shared merge step every site's results pass through) were discarding almost every result whose FILM TITLE doesn't literally contain the query words - even though the site's own /?s= search had already correctly matched it by cast/performer name or genre tag (confirmed live: a performer-name query legitimately surfaced films she's credited in, and a genre-word query legitimately surfaced every film tagged with it). Removed both redundant local re-checks for Adult - confirmed live this took a real performer search from 2 movies to 17, and a real genre search from 1 movie to 33, both correctly labeled by title. Then audited every site this touches (13 direct sources plus the 24-site Scenes tube registry) by comparing real vs deliberately nonsensical queries: two sites (hd.xmovix.net, hqporner.com) turned out to return byte-for-byte identical results regardless of what's actually searched - a genuinely broken/non-functional search on their end, now confirmed and dropped from Adult's unified search (their own browse/listing screens are unaffected) since they were injecting the same handful of unrelated titles into every single search. Every other source audited (22 of 24 Scenes sites, plus freeo/xxxsc/panda/mango/spvip/sf/paradise/pxp) genuinely changes its results based on the query - confirmed and left as-is.
v2.3.510 - Fixed Adult stream-search results showing only a bare host name ("Doodstream", "Mixdrop", etc.) with no way to tell which movie each result actually belonged to - confirmed live by running a real search and inspecting the actual returned labels. The matched film's own title was being read only for a log line, never attached to the stream entry itself, in both of the two places that build these results (adult_streams.py's own site-search merge, and scraper_sources.py's supplementary title-scraper merge). Every stream result now carries the movie's own title alongside the host name (e.g. "Movie Title - Doodstream") instead of just the host name, so a search returning several different matching titles (or the same title's several mirrors) is actually distinguishable in the picker.
v2.3.509 - Fixed a real reported bug: searching Adult for a performer name (e.g. a scene never searched before, cold cache) could return zero movies even though the underlying scrape/match logic was completely correct - confirmed live the direct search+match chain reliably finds real, playable results in 10-20s when called with no time pressure. Root cause was a timing/architecture bug, not a scraping or matching bug: adult_streams.search_by_title() (the function backing the Adult unified search box's "stream sites" branch) has its own internal ~20s soft cutoff for searching its ~20 sites, THEN calls scraper_sources.search_all_scrapers() as a second, effectively unbounded phase (that function has its own separate ~35s internal cutoff) - pushing this whole function's worst-case duration past 50s. But it's called from afdb_router.py's unified search box under an OUTER 20s deadline that abandons the ENTIRE result if not back in time, so on a cold cache this second phase alone was enough to blow the outer deadline and silently discard everything, every time. Tightened both phases (12s + a newly-added independent 6s cap on the scraper_sources phase, replacing its previous unbounded call) so the whole function reliably finishes with real margin under that outer 20s window - confirmed live with a genuinely cold cache: 10.6s total, real playable results returned.
v2.3.508 - Investigated a reported Adult scraper issue (watchpornfree.info) end to end. Site itself is fine - confirmed live its listing/detail page markup and its title-based search (which already matches performer names and genre keywords via WordPress's own search, e.g. a performer-name query for a real scene returns a real, correctly-matched hit) are all still working exactly as scraped. The real, fixable bug found: watchpornfree.info's detail pages (and every other stream-scraping source sharing the same filter - pornwatch.ws, speedporn.net, xxxscenes.net, xxxmoviestream.org, pandamovies.org, mangoporn.net, plus scraper_sources.py's shared sources) unconditionally discarded nitroflare/rapidgator/frdl.io/uploaded/keep2share links as "unusable premium lockers" - but Real-Debrid's (and AllDebrid's) own unrestrict API genuinely supports unlocking most of these directly (confirmed live: ResolveURL's own installed realdebrid.py plugin declares domains=['*'], meaning it forwards ANY host straight to Real-Debrid's API rather than needing a hardcoded supported-host list here). These links are now only discarded when NO debrid service is paired at all; with one paired, they're kept and handed to the normal resolve step like any other stream link - directly increasing the pool of real playable results a performer/genre/title search on any of these sites can surface. Also batch-verified every other adult scraper source's base site is currently reachable; two came back genuinely broken on their own end rather than a scraper bug - swingerpornfun.com is walled by a real Cloudflare Turnstile JS challenge (same un-fixable-from-Python-code class of block already documented elsewhere in this addon), and pelisxporno.net is returning its own WordPress fatal error page - neither is fixable client-side, flagged rather than silently left broken.
v2.3.507 - Added WeTrakr as a third watch-tracking service, alongside the existing Trakt and SIMKL pairing (Settings -> Premium Services -> "Pair with WeTrakr" - scan the QR code or enter the short code, no client id/secret/registration needed at all, confirmed against the real installed script.wetrakr Kodi add-on's own source since WeTrakr has no public API docs). New wetrakr_auth.py/wetrakr_sync.py mirror trakt_sync.py's/simkl_sync.py's exact function names so every existing call site (mark-watched, scrobble start/pause/stop, Continue Watching's dismiss/priority-provider logic) works identically - reshaped internally to WeTrakr's real API shape, which is architecturally different from Trakt/SIMKL: a single webhook endpoint (not a REST resource collection) with the access token embedded in the URL path rather than an Authorization header, and no GET endpoint at all to query saved progress back (unlike SIMKL's /sync/playback) - so WeTrakr contributes scrobbling/mark-watched but never becomes the source for cross-device resume, same honest limitation this addon's own Trakt integration already has for its own no-equivalent-endpoint case. Same adult-content safeguard as Trakt/SIMKL: only real tt-prefixed IMDB ids are ever sent, so opaque adult source keys never reach WeTrakr regardless of pairing state.
v2.3.506 - Confirmed and handled a real ADE catalog structure per user report: adultdvdempire.com lists a DVD edition ("-porn-movies.html") and a separate on-demand/streaming edition ("-porn-videos.html") of the SAME title under two DIFFERENT numeric product ids (verified live: "Orgy Masters 7" alone has id 1735474 for its DVD listing and 1736457 for its on-demand listing). request_sources.py's Adult Requests fallback lookup previously only checked ADE's single top-ranked search result against our known adc_id - now checks every exact-title candidate ADE's search returns, so a correct adc_id that happens to be the "other" edition's id (the one ADE's search doesn't rank first) still validates and pulls full metadata, instead of being wrongly treated as a miss. Note this doesn't fix the specific "Orgy Masters 7" entry already in the JSON - confirmed live its recorded adc_id (1676457) matches NEITHER of the two real ids, so that one specific id looks like a data-entry typo that needs manual correction, not a code issue.
v2.3.505 - Fixed Adult Requests still not showing posters for some titles (confirmed live via a real screenshot - "Thr3e 11" had cast names but blank/mask-icon photos and no poster at all). Root cause: ADE's own site returns a genuine HTTP 415 for this addon's plain CDN-formula cover-art guess on some films, and the real fallback (that film's actual og:image tag, already being fetched for description/cast) was silently never matching either - its newer pages write the tag as property='og:image' with single quotes while this addon's regex only matched the double-quoted style, so a real, working cover was sitting right there in the page and never got picked up. Fixed the regex to accept either quote style (confirmed live: 9 of the current 10 real Adult Requests entries now resolve to a real, working HTTP 200 cover this way) and wired the corrected thumb/fanart into both the real in-app Requests screen (as a lazy poster/backdrop override, same mechanism Sports already uses for venue photos) and the plain directory-listing path. The one entry that still won't resolve ("Orgy Masters 7") has a data problem, not a code one - confirmed live that ADE's own site doesn't recognize adc_id 1676457 at all (redirects to its homepage), while a real search for that exact title finds it under id 1735474 instead; flagging rather than silently guessing, since correcting an id from an unvalidated title-search match would violate this addon's own "never trust an unverified id" rule.
v2.3.504 - The orchestrator's requests_movies/tv/adult.json files now each carry 10 blank placeholder slots (e.g. {"adc_id": "", "title": "", "urls": []}) so a new request can just be filled in directly without hand-typing the JSON shape from scratch every time. Added a filter (request_sources.py's new _has_source() check) so every getter (get_requested_movies/tv/adult) drops any entry with no real url before anything else in the addon ever sees it - blank slots never show up as an empty listing in the Requests screens, never get offered as a search/playback match, and are completely invisible until actually filled in with a real link, exactly as intended. Also fixed two new Adult entries ("Orgy Masters 7", "In-Laws") that had the same missing-comma JSON mistake documented in earlier releases - both parse correctly now and pull full ADE metadata like every other entry.
v2.3.503 - Fixed Adult Requests inconsistently pulling full metadata - confirmed live via real screenshots that some titles (e.g. "Revenge of a Daughter", "An Orgy for Cassie") showed only cover art with no description/cast while others worked fine. Root cause: the previous fix searched ADE by title and only trusted the result when its id matched our own known adc_id, but that title search itself sometimes failed to find/rank the right film even though the id we already had was completely correct. Replaced it with a much more reliable id-only lookup: confirmed live that ADE's own site redirects a bare numeric product id straight to that exact film's real detail page (a wrong id instead redirects to the homepage, giving a clean way to tell success from failure) - no title matching involved at all now, so every entry with a real adc_id (which is all of them, by schema) gets full data every time. Also found and fixed two related gaps while verifying this against real film pages: year and runtime were coming back blank on newer-format ADE pages whose markup doesn't match the older patterns this addon's parser looked for - now falls back to that page's own og:video:release_date/duration meta tags, which are always present; and film descriptions were showing raw unescaped HTML (literally """ instead of a quote mark) - now properly decoded. Verified live across all 8 real current Requests entries: all 8 now return a full description, complete cast list, studio, year, and runtime.

Now, every time a cached movie/TV detail is about to be reused, its release/air date is checked against today - if that date has passed but the cached status still doesn't reflect it, this one entry is treated as a miss and silently re-fetched fresh (then cached correctly for its full normal window again). Verified against 6 real and synthetic cases including the exact bug pattern, and confirmed live against the actual currently-cached data this addon has right now - already-correct entries are completely unaffected, only a genuinely stale pre-release snapshot ever triggers the extra fetch.

Android also blocks ADB/file-manager access to the addon's own private data directory, so there was no way to force this without the app itself doing it - this button does it from inside Kodi's own Settings UI, no ADB or file access needed. v2.3.223 - Fixed a regression from v2.3.220's Adult title-cleaning: the bare word "XXX" was being stripped out of every title anywhere it appeared, but that word is frequently a real, intentional part of adult film titles (e.g. "The Odyssey: A XXX Parody" - a parody title genre convention), not junk. Stripping it mangled the title before it was used to cross-reference the real catalog for high-quality cover art, so that lookup stopped matching and posters fell back to nothing - confirmed live. Now only strips "XXX" when it's clearly its own bracketed tag, e.g. "(XXX)" or "[XXX]" with nothing else inside, which doesn't collide with a title that legitimately contains the word. v2.3.222 - Fixed Adult section listings collapsing to almost nothing after a few hours of real use (confirmed live: New Releases went from showing real content to showing none at all). Root cause was in the has-a-source filter added in v2.3.220: it decided whether to hide a title based on a passive index of whatever detail pages happened to already be cached from past browsing - early on that index is empty (lenient, shows everything), but after enough browsing it becomes non-empty while still being nowhere near a complete picture, and the filter started treating "never actually checked" the same as "confirmed no source", hiding almost everything. Fixed at the source: added a real, separate "confirmed no source" record that's only written after an actual search for that exact title comes back empty, and the filter now only hides a title once that's genuinely happened - titles it hasn't gotten to yet keep showing immediately like before, and only get hidden once really confirmed absent, so the list starts accurate and gets more accurate over time instead of collapsing. Also found (separate issue, not yet fixed): Adult DVD Empire's movie trailers are dead through this addon's existing trailer URL formula - checked a real, current film page directly and that entire domain/path pattern doesn't exist anymore; the site has moved trailers to a different domain requiring a per-scene ID this addon doesn't currently track, not just a movie ID. Needs its own scraper work to properly fix - flagged for a follow-up rather than a rushed fix tonight. v2.3.221 - EMERGENCY FIX: v2.3.220's bytecode-only build completely broke the addon - confirmed live via kodi.log that every single plugin:// call failed with "ImportError: bad magic number in 'resources'". The bytecode was correctly compiled for Python 3.11.9 (verified before shipping), but Kodi's own bundled Python 3.11 build on this device uses a different internal magic number stamp than standalone Python 3.11.9 - the exact version-mismatch risk flagged before attempting this, just at a finer-grained level (same Kodi major version, different bundled interpreter patch) than expected. Reverted immediately to plain, uncompiled source - identical code to v2.3.220, just not bytecode-compiled - to restore a working addon. No further obfuscation attempts until a build approach can be verified against Kodi's actual bundled interpreter directly rather than a same-numbered standalone Python install. v2.3.220 - Fixed CFL (and College Football/CFB) missing from the Sports menu entirely: confirmed live that CFL games were showing up with nowhere to actually navigate to them, because a dedup check meant to stop TheSportsDB's raw sport list from adding a redundant generic "American Football" menu entry was also (wrongly) applied to this addon's OWN curated category list - since NFL, CFB, and CFL are all classified as the same TheSportsDB sport ("American Football"), and NFL happens to be listed first, CFB and CFL were being silently skipped out of the menu every time, as if they didn't exist. Also fixed the actual cause of CFL games showing up mixed into the NFL listing itself (confirmed live: a real CFL game and a European League of Football game both appeared inside NFL) - the supplementary schedule source has no per-league split for American football, so it was merged in unfiltered for whichever of NFL/CFB/CFL happened to have a menu entry; now filtered by each game's real league name before merging, so NFL only shows NFL, CFL only shows CFL, etc. Both bugs together also explain why a real CFL game's own stream links weren't found when played from the (wrong) NFL section - the wrong sport was being passed to every stream resolver, none of which know to check CFL's actual listings when told to look for NFL. Fixed a narrow but real race condition behind the home screen occasionally failing to load a section on the first click (confirmed live, matched reports it "works on retry"): a background thread that pushes freshly-loaded data into the home screen can land mid-navigation and throw against an already-closing window; tightened from both sides so the window signals it's closing before doing anything else, and the background thread re-checks immediately before touching it. Also fixed the Sports section's page title showing a broken/unreadable placeholder character in the breadcrumb (e.g. "Videos / Starfleet / [?] Boxing") - a stadium/hockey emoji in the category title that this Kodi build's skin font can't render; replaced with plain text. Adult section: film titles are now cleaned of common scraping junk (duplicate year tags, resolution/release tags) before being displayed or used to check for a stream source - a mismatched messy title on one side of that check could cause a real, working film to be wrongly dropped as "no source"; the New Releases/Recently Added/Best Sellers listings were also found to skip the has-a-source check entirely (unlike every other Adult listing), so titles with no actual stream anywhere were shown and dead-ended on click - now filtered the same as everywhere else. Performer/actor search in the Adult section's unified search was a stub that always returned nothing ("no actor search API - skip for now") - built a real one backed by a cached full name index from the site's own per-letter actor pages. New sports stream source added (livetv902.me / livetv.sx family): covers a wide range of sports and leagues this addon didn't have a source for before; found via live investigation that its "alieztv"-type mirrors resolve through a plain, unobfuscated JS call to a real HLS URL - no WASM/P2P wall like embed.st - verified against a real live CFL game. Note: this source's availability was inconsistent in testing (worked reliably in some passes, not in others, without a clear cause) - it's wired in as a supplementary source alongside everything else, so it simply contributes nothing extra when it's not available rather than causing any problem. v2.3.219 - Fixed MLB Network and NHL Network (24/7 channels) not playing: verified live that daddylive.mov's signing CDN (fiveo4.casadenoval.uk) started rejecting every request with a bare 403, even a freshly-decoded, correctly-signed, not-yet-expired URL with the right Referer - this looked at first like the same un-fixable TLS-fingerprint wall documented elsewhere in this changelog for Cloudflare Turnstile, but confirmed by direct testing it isn't: the CDN now also requires the Sec-Fetch-Dest/Mode/Site "fetch metadata" headers a real browser always sends and that neither our scraper nor, importantly, Kodi's own player ever did - simply adding them (both to our own verification check and onto the URL Kodi's player actually opens, via the same header pipe-syntax already used elsewhere for Referer/User-Agent) resolves it. Also added a live-verification step this resolver was missing entirely: previously, once a mirror's obfuscated blob decoded into something that merely looked like a URL, that URL was handed straight to Kodi's player with no check that it would actually serve - now it's fetched and confirmed to return a real #EXTM3U playlist first, so a mirror that decodes but 403s (this exact bug) or serves an expired/dead link gets correctly skipped in favor of the next mirror instead of crashing playback. v2.3.218 - Fixed Adult section kicking the user all the way out of the addon on click, same class of bug as the Sports crash-out fixed in v2.3.216/217, but guaranteed to happen every time instead of intermittently: entering the Adult section shows a PIN entry prompt if one is set, and that prompt was popping up in the middle of the same window-activation sequence a Sports click goes through - any blocking dialog shown at that exact moment can make Kodi abandon the transition. The PIN check now happens before the home screen even starts navigating away, not during it. Also fixed a related bug found while fixing this: the "only ask for the PIN once per session" behavior never actually worked, because this addon runs with reuselanguageinvoker off (a fresh Python process per call, confirmed in addon.xml) - the old code stored the unlock flag in a plain in-memory variable that reset on every single click, silently re-prompting for the PIN every time despite the setting's own description promising otherwise. Now persisted properly so it actually only asks once. Also: the home screen's focus-highlight border around the selected poster is noticeably larger now - the previous release's ~2% bump turned out to be too subtle to see; also enlarged the matching per-row focus borders (there were two overlapping highlight mechanisms in the skin, only one of which was resized last time). v2.3.217 - Follow-up to v2.3.216's navigation fix, based on further live testing on the Firestick: the previous release stopped the "kicked all the way out of the addon" symptom, but a deeper live test showed the fix's own two-step handoff (jump to an empty placeholder screen first, then swap in the real category a moment later) could still get stuck - the second step silently failing to fire, leaving the user stranded on a permanently empty screen instead of the Sports (or Movies/TV/Live TV/Adult) page they clicked. Replaced that two-step handoff with a single direct jump straight to the clicked category, removing the fragile middle step entirely. Trade-off: Back out of a category may now return to Kodi's previous screen instead of this addon's home screen in some cases, rather than a category that may not load at all - confirmed working live against Sports. v2.3.216 - Fixed a real crash-on-navigate bug found by live-testing on the Firestick: clicking Sports (or any top-nav category) in the home screen could silently kick the user all the way out of the addon back to Kodi's own Add-ons screen, with no error dialog. Also: the dependency-check prompt (offers to install ResolveURL) was re-running on every single in-app navigation click, not just on first launch - could pop a blocking install prompt mid-navigation for no reason connected to what was actually clicked; now only runs when Home is genuinely (re)launching. Also: the home screen's focus-highlight border around the selected poster is now slightly larger (~2%) per user request, for better visibility. v2.3.215 - Fixed three real skin-navigation bugs found by live-testing on the Firestick with ADB: (1) an unprompted auto-relaunch, where backing all the way out to Kodi's own Add-ons screen would spontaneously reopen Starfleet's home a moment later with zero input - root cause was the addon's own root action relaunching Home on ANY visit to its plugin:// root with no fresh lock file present, including background metadata queries from Kodi/the active Kodi skin (e.g. Add-ons tile widgets), not just genuine user launches; now only relaunches when the Videos window is actually the one on screen. (2) The home screen's hero banner (title/plot/Play/More Info) could get stuck showing a previous section's item when switching to a section with no content yet (e.g. Live TV with no favorites saved) - it's now cleared instead of left stale. (3) Moving left/right at the very edge of a carousel row could unexpectedly jump focus to the top nav bar instead of stopping at the row - the row lists were missing their own left/right wrap targets, letting Kodi's automatic proximity navigation take over.
v2.3.214 - Added a new working stream resolver: streame.center, a shared embed backend used by several front-end sites (e.g. powerstreams.site, realsportshd.buzz) that a raw embed link alone can't play (its ch##.php/hls.php pages need a decrypt.php exchange first, done automatically now) - verified live against a real MLB game. Rather than write one scraper per front-end site (most of them have no real schedule of their own to scrape - one 403s outright, another is just a static link directory), this runs as a universal post-processing step across every existing source (StreamsEast, CrackStreams, etc), so any sport those sources already cover gets this fix automatically the moment one of them happens to route through streame.center. Also fixed the repo's own landing page (index.html) linking to a stale repository.starfleet-1.0.11.zip instead of the current 1.0.13 - a fresh install via that page was pulling the old repository add-on even though addons.xml itself was already correct.
v2.3.213 - Fixed CrackStreams returning 0 events for every sport, every time: its event-listing page was being fetched at /league/mlbstreams (etc.), which is a 404 - the site moved to /category/mlb/ (etc.) a while back, and even that correct page no longer has any scrapable per-game links in its static HTML (JS-rendered listing, like most of this ecosystem now). Rather than reverse-engineer another discovery API, this now builds the event page URL directly from the two team names in the title (CrackStreams' own URL pattern is the predictable /stream/<team>-vs-<team>, tried in both team orders) - verified live against a real game that this correctly finds the page and extracts its actual stream list, where before it always found nothing. Note: depending on the specific event, CrackStreams' own links may route through the same embed.st-family WASM-gated hosts documented as unfixable in previous releases - that's a limitation of whichever embed provider that event happens to use, not of this fix.
v2.3.212 - New working stream source for MLB/NBA/NHL/NFL: mlb24all.ir and its sibling sites (nba24all.ir, nhl24all.ir, nfl24all.ir) were already listed in this addon's own code as a planned source, but the implementation was dead - it scraped for HTML anchor links that stopped existing once those sites became client-rendered apps, and it was never actually wired into the stream picker to begin with. Replaced it with a real implementation found via live network inspection: these sites run a clean, unauthenticated JSON API (GET .../api/v3/stateshot for the game/team catalogue, POST .../api/v2/generate_stream_info for a direct playable HLS link) - no login, no obfuscation, no WASM, just a straightforward API call. Verified live against an in-progress Blue Jays vs Rays game: returns real, independently-confirmed-working ESPN Home/Away broadcast links. This runs alongside every other source in the same merged link dialog, so a game covered by this source now shows up as extra "Link N" options next to StreamsEast/DaddyLive/etc.
v2.3.211 - Fixed a real crash-on-play bug found by testing the Blue Jays game live on-device: the DaddyLive/TVNow24/7-channel resolver (used for the MLB/NHL Network channels and as the supplementary source merged into every sport event's link dialog) would, when none of a channel's mirrors could be decoded, hand back the raw unresolved mirror page URL on the theory that ResolveURL "might know it" â€” instead Kodi got a plain HTML page and crashed immediately with "error probing input format". Now returns nothing for that channel instead, so it's correctly dropped from the dialog rather than offered as a guaranteed-broken option. Also discovered and wired up a much more reliable resolution path for one whole class of these mirrors: some daddylive.mov mirrors point at tvnow247.top's own /embed/<channel> page, which used to fail outright (it's a client-rendered app with nothing scrapable in its HTML) â€” found via live network inspection that its player calls a clean JSON API (chat.cfbu247.sbs/api/resolve-dlstream) to get its real stream, so that's tried first now, with a live-playlist check before accepting it (a couple of channels' upstreams turned out to be genuinely offline right now, verified directly â€” not a scraper bug, just those specific feeds being down). StreamsEast (embed.st) links are confirmed to depend on a WASM+P2P ticket-exchange system with no static stream URL anywhere in the page - verified via live browser inspection that even a real browser only gets a playable stream after running embed.st's own obfuscated code, which can't be replicated from a Kodi Python addon - left as-is this release since that's a limitation of that specific host, not something scraping can fix.
v2.3.210 - Fixed MLB (and every sport's) StreamsEast source: streamseast.is is dead (the domain no longer resolves at all); the site moved to streameasti.is with a different URL structure (no numeric event id, irregular section-name pluralization) and a different embed mechanism (source buttons carry a base64-encoded URL in a data-s attribute, swapped into the player by a JS click handler â€” the iframe's own src is always blank in the raw HTML, so the old scraper found nothing). Updated the domain, URL patterns, and added the data-s extraction, so StreamsEast now contributes real "Link N" options again for every sport, not just MLB. Verified against a real live Blue Jays game: get_event_streams now returns 3 StreamsEast links + 3 more from the TVNow247/DaddyLive source added in v2.3.209, all 6 shown together in one sequentially-numbered dialog (this merging was already automatic â€” fixing the two sources was the actual work). v2.3.209 - New: MLB Network 24/7 channel added to the MLB section â€” selecting it shows a Link 1/2/3 picker across three known-good daddylive.mov mirrors. New: full Live TV source added â€” TVNow247 (500+ channels scraped from tvnow247.top, adult channels excluded). New: live sports events scraped from tvnow247.top/schedule.json are now merged into each sport's event listing and used as a supplementary stream source everywhere, categorized by sport automatically. Fixed a real bug found while building these: the daddylive.mov channel resolver assumed every mirror-list JSON entry has the same {name,url} shape, but some pages use {name,id,url} with an extra field in between â€” entries in that shape were silently never matching. Also fixed: numeric-only channel ids (this addon's own MLB "399" test case, plus most of TVNow247's catalogue) were falling back to parsing the page's title tag for the real channel name, but title formats vary wildly ("Free X Live...", "Watch X Online...", "X Live Stream Free...") and that guess was unreliable â€” callers that already know the real name (the new TV channel list, the new events scraper) now pass it through explicitly instead of guessing, which took random-sample channel resolution from 0% to 100% in testing. v2.3.208 - v2.3.207 verified live: NHL Network now resolves and plays (confirmed reaching video decode), and Back from Movies/TV Shows/etc now correctly returns to the home screen. This release fixes the one remaining piece: the carousel focus highlight still wasn't showing, because the id=90 overlay control had a hardcoded <visible>false</visible> in the skin XML â€” Kodi re-evaluates XML visible conditions continuously, which silently overrides/no-ops any Python setVisible(True) call. Removed the XML condition; visibility is now owned entirely by home.py (explicitly hidden on init, shown/positioned on focus). v2.3.207 - NHL Network 24/7 channel still didn't play after v2.3.205's onhockey.tv fix, because onhockey.tv's own proxy for that channel (daddylive.php) is dead (404). Now resolves directly via daddylive.mov's channel mirror list, decoding the obfuscated embed script one mirror tier uses to get a fresh signed .m3u8. Also: fixed Adult section movie posters occasionally showing a neighboring film's cover art (nearest-match bug in the cover-art scraper). Also: home screen carousel focus highlight (the orange selection border on Movies/TV/etc rows) now actually renders â€” it was never appearing on some devices/Kodi builds even though selection itself worked. Also: Back from a section (Movies/TV Shows/etc) now correctly returns to the home screen instead of exiting past the addon into Kodi's own Videos section. v2.3.206 - Fix free/non-debrid streams not resolving: script.module.resolveurl was marked optional and pinned to a stale version (5.1.28) that was never actually hosted anywhere, so it was silently never installed. Now required, bumped to the real published 5.1.206, and pulled from the repository's new smrzips repo dir. v2.3.205 - Fix NHL Network (Sports section) not playing: onhockey.tv's live-channel page (used for the 24/7 NHL Network stream) embeds its player via JS config (src/file/source: "...m3u8") or a same-domain proxy iframe, not the plain stream links the scraper was looking for. Added JS-embedded m3u8 detection and a same-domain iframe follow-through, matching the extraction already used successfully for this exact channel in the Live TV section.

extension.description: Elementum is a torrent finding and streaming engine. It doesn't go on torrent websites for legal reasons. However, it calls specially crafted add-ons (called providers) that are installed separately. This project is a fork of the well known, but no longer maintained Pulsar/Quasar projects from steeve and scakemyer. NOTE: install plugin.video.elementum-0.1.114.zip from the repository first, then manually install the matching plugin.video.elementum-0.1.114.<platform>.zip on top for your device's platform (e.g. windows_x64, android_arm64, linux_x64) and restart Kodi - binaries are split into per-platform zips to stay under GitHub's 100MB file size limit.
